title: Kilclone, County Meath
standfirst: One deed memorial names a compact Glasco family at Kilclone. It is unusually direct evidence, but it gives no bridge to the other Irish clusters.
question: Can further Meath evidence identify the Kilclone family without merging it into Dublin, Rathdowney or Ulster?
answer: The memorial directly names Patrick Glasco as father of James, Richard and William. That establishes a local sibling group. It does not provide Patrick's origins, the sons' later lives, or a relationship to any similarly named Irish household.

chapters.title: A stated father and three sons
body: The Kilclone memorial is the documentary anchor: Patrick Glasco is named as father of James, Richard and William.
The direct wording is stronger than a shared surname or parish, but it is a small local family record rather than a wider pedigree.

chapters.title: No demonstrated continuation
body: No maintained record links this family to the Dublin trade group, Rathdowney material, Ulster occurrences or a Scottish baptism.
Those comparisons should remain search leads until a record names a relationship, succession or shared holding.

clusters.title: Patrick Glasco's named family
